title: Emergency Situations
description: Learn to get help in emergencies and report problems
objectives: Describe what happened (There is a fire / Someone is hurt)
Give your address and location clearly

phrases: There is a fire / an accident
I need an ambulance / the police / the fire department
target_language.grammar_pattern:
There is + emergency
Someone is + condition
I need + service
My address is + location

Examples:
- There is a fire
- Someone is hurt
- I need an ambulance
- My address is 250 Oak Street

grammar_patterns.label: Giving your location
examples: I am at the grocery store on Main Street

story.context: You smell smoke in your apartment building. You see fire coming from an apartment down the hall. You call 911.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: There is a fire! In my apartment building!

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: 250 Oak Street. It is an apartment building.

dialogue.speaker: Operator
dialogue.text: What floor is the fire on?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I don't know. I don't see anyone. There is a lot of smoke.

dialogue.speaker: Operator
dialogue.text: Okay. The fire department is on the way. Get out of the building now. Do not use the elevator. Use the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Operator
dialogue.text: Go outside and wait for the fire trucks. Stay on the phone with me.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay. I am going down the stairs now. Please hurry!

dialogue.speaker: Operator
dialogue.text: They are almost there. Stay calm and keep moving.

listening.question: Listen: What is the emergency?
listening.explanation: The caller says 'There is a fire in my building!'

listening.question: Listen: What does the caller need?
listening.explanation: The caller says 'I need an ambulance. Someone is hurt.'

listening.question: Listen: What does the operator tell the person to do?
listening.explanation: The operator says 'Get out of the building and wait outside.'

speaking.title: Task 1: Call 911
speaking.instruction: Record yourself calling 911. Say: there is a fire, give your address, and say which floor.
speaking.example: There is a fire! My address is 250 Oak Street. It is on the fourth floor. Please hurry!

speaking.title: Task 2: Emergency conversation
speaking.instruction: Record a full 911 call where someone is hurt and you need an ambulance.
speaking.example:
Operator: 911. What is your emergency?
You: Someone is hurt. I need an ambulance.
Operator: What is your address?
You: 250 Oak Street, apartment 4B.
Operator: Help is on the way.
You: Please hurry! Thank you.

writing.title: Task 1: Emergency sentences
writing.instruction: Write 5 sentences you might say in an emergency. Use 'There is...', 'Someone is...', and 'I need...'
writing.example:
1. There is a fire!
2. Someone is hurt.
3. I need an ambulance.
4. My address is 250 Oak Street.
5. Please hurry!

writing.title: Task 2: Write a 911 call
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (8-10 lines) where you call 911 to report a car accident.
writing.example:
Operator: 911. What is your emergency?
You: There is a car accident!
Operator: Where?
You: On Main Street, near the grocery store.
Operator: Is anyone hurt?
You: Yes. Someone is hurt.
Operator: I am sending an ambulance.
You: Please hurry!
Operator: Stay with the person. Help is coming.
You: Okay. Thank you.

sections.title: Reporting with 'There is'
sections.question: How do we report that something is happening?
sections.explanation: We use 'There is + a/an + [thing]' to report that something exists or is happening. In emergencies, we say this urgently. Notice: 'a fire' but 'an accident' — we use 'an' before vowel sounds (a, e, i, o, u).

sections.title: Describing conditions with 'Someone is'
sections.question: How do we describe what is wrong with a person?
sections.explanation: We use 'Someone is + [condition]' when we see a person who needs help but don't know their name. If you know the person, use their name: 'Marcus is hurt.'

sections.title: Important safety words
sections.question: What are the most important emergency words?
sections.explanation: In America, call 911 for any emergency. The operator will send the right help: an ambulance for medical emergencies, the fire department for fires, or the police for crimes or danger. Always give your address clearly.

quiz.question: There is a fire in your building. What number do you call?
quiz.explanation: 911 is the emergency number in America. Call 911 for fires, accidents, and medical emergencies.

quiz.question: Someone is very sick and needs to go to the hospital. You say:
quiz.explanation: An ambulance takes sick or hurt people to the hospital.

quiz.question: The 911 operator asks 'What is your address?' You say:
quiz.explanation: Give your full address — street number, street name, and apartment number — so help can find you.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: There is ___ accident on Main Street.
quiz.explanation: We use 'an' before words that start with a vowel sound. 'An accident' is correct. 'A' is used before consonant sounds, 'the' is for specific things, and no article would leave the sentence incomplete here.

quiz.question: The operator says 'Do not use the elevator. Use the stairs.' Why?
options: The elevator can stop during a fire — it is dangerous
quiz.explanation: During a fire, elevators can stop working and trap you. Always use the stairs during a fire.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: Someone ___ hurt.
quiz.explanation: 'Someone' is singular, so we use 'is'. 'Someone is hurt.'

quiz.question: You see a car accident. What do you say to the operator?
quiz.explanation: 'There is an accident' correctly reports what you see. Then give the location.

quiz.question: Which is MOST important to tell the 911 operator?
quiz.explanation: The most important things are: what happened (fire, accident, someone hurt) and where you are (your address). This helps them send the right help to the right place.

quiz.question: Write a 6-line 911 call where you report that someone fell and is hurt at the grocery store.
quiz.explanation: Your conversation should include: calling 911, saying what happened, the location, and asking for help.

quiz.question: Write your real address. Then write 2 sentences about what you would say if you needed to call 911.
quiz.explanation: Knowing how to say your address in English is very important for emergencies. Practice so you can say it quickly and clearly.
